research.domain: Image generation base models / checkpoints (text-to-image) — re-download guide for RTX 5090 / 32 GB VRAM, ComfyUI, mid-2026
research.notes: RIG FIT: All 9 listed models run on the RTX 5090 (32 GB). The big 2026 shift since your last setup is the FLUX.2 family (Nov 2025 / Jan 2026) and a wave of fast Apache-2.0 Chinese bases (Z-Image, Qwen-Image-2512). COMMERCIAL-SAFETY for game assets is the decisive axis here — the field has bifurcated: (a) truly permissive Apache/MIT bases you can sell assets from freely — Z-Image-Turbo, Qwen-Image/2512, Chroma1-HD, FLUX.2-klein-4B, HiDream-I1; vs (b) non-commercial or conditional bases — FLUX.2-dev (NON-COMMERCIAL, like FLUX.1-dev before it), SD3.5 (free only under $1M revenue), and most anime bases. TOP PICKS for your dual use: (1) Qwen-Image-2512 — best all-rounder, Apache 2.0, unbeatable text-in-image for marketing, strong photoreal, trainable; (2) Z-Image-Turbo — Apache 2.0, sub-second, #1 open model on Artificial Analysis Image Arena, the new daily-driver; (3) Chroma1-HD — Apache 2.0 FLUX-quality base purpose-built as a LoRA/finetune target = your commercial-safe game-asset workhorse; (4) Illustrious XL v2.0 — commercial-OK anime/illustration base with the deepest Danbooru-tag LoRA ecosystem. AVOID for paid game assets unless you clear licensing: FLUX.2-dev (non-commercial weights), NoobAI (non-commercial), Pony V7 (Pony License blocks inference-service/>$1M/pro-video). LoRA-TRAINABILITY note: SDXL-lineage (Illustrious, Juggernaut) and Chroma have the most mature, cheapest LoRA training; FLUX.2/Qwen LoRA training works but is heavier (24 GB+). VERSION CAVEATS: numbers like FLUX.2-dev fitting 32 GB assume 4-bit (bnb/NVFP4) quantization — full bf16 32B needs offload; this is normal and ComfyUI handles it. Pony V7 launched Oct 2025 on AuraFlow and early community reception was mixed vs the entrenched Illustrious/NoobAI ecosystems — verify current community checkpoints before committing. All facts pulled from official HF/GitHub model cards + reputable 2026 coverage (VentureBeat, the-decoder, MarkTechPost) as of 2026-06-02; my training cutoff predates klein/Z-Image/2512 so these were confirmed live via web.

verify.summary: All 10 primary models resolve via retrieval and 9 are confirmed (8 outright, 1 with a minor benchmark-attribution nuance that itself checks out). The collection is current and well-licensed for a 32 GB card. Strongest verifications: Z-Image-Turbo's "#1 open-weights, beats FLUX.2-dev/HunyuanImage 3.0/Qwen-Image" claim is independently confirmed by Artificial Analysis's own post (the HF card calls the board "Alibaba/AI Arena", but the researcher's AA-Arena attribution is correct). Qwen-Image-2512 is a real standalone checkpoint (not just a Space) and the HF card explicitly claims "strongest open-source text-to-image model" on AI Arena. Qwen-Image=20B MMDiT, SD3.5 Large=8.1B MMDiT, FLUX.2-dev=32B non-commercial, FLUX.2-klein-4B=Apache 4B ~13GB, Chroma1-HD=8.9B FLUX.1-schnell-derived Apache, HiDream-I1=17B MIT with Full/Dev/Fast tiers — all confirmed. License-wise everything is accurate including the tricky ones (FLUX.2-dev non-commercial, SD3.5 Stability Community License <$1M, Illustrious OpenRAIL-M conditional, Juggernaut RAIL++-M conditional). Minor data-point notes: Juggernaut's "18M+ downloads" is a family-level figure (the Civitai page hosts all versions); the page surfaced 2.6M for one variant, but RunDiffusion's own 18M+ family claim backs the researcher. Extras: mostly real and well-chosen, but note Pony V7 base is built on AuraFlow (Apache 2), NOT SDXL — calling it an "anime-base" is fine but it is not SDXL-lineage; and the FLUX.1-schnell extra has a copy-paste wrong URL (points to Chroma1-HD). Several extras cite third-party blog/aggregator URLs rather than canonical model pages. Coverage is excellent; the few omissions I'd flag are HunyuanImage 3.0, Lumina-Image 2.0, and a Qwen-Image-Edit/editing-base entry.

verdicts.note: Both repos resolve. Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 is a genuine standalone checkpoint (not merely a Space), Apache 2.0, and its HF card explicitly claims 'currently the strongest open-source text-to-image model' on AI Arena with 10k+ blind evals, plus the exact improvements cited (photoreal faces/wrinkles, natural detail, better text). Base Qwen-Image = 20B MMDiT confirmed via Apache-2.0 card + multiple independent sources. 16GB min for the 20B model is plausible only with FP8/quantization, which is the standard 5090 path — fine.
verdicts.specs_plausible_detail: 20B at 16GB requires FP8/offload; achievable on 32GB card comfortably.

verdicts.note: Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo resolves: 6B, Apache-2.0, S3-DiT (Scalable Single-Stream DiT), 8 NFE distilled, fits 16GB, bilingual text — all confirmed on the HF card. The headline claim (#1 open-source on Artificial Analysis Image Arena, beating FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage 3.0, Qwen-Image) is INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by Artificial Analysis's own announcement. Nuance: the HF card itself names the board 'Alibaba AI Arena', but the researcher's AA-Arena attribution is the correct/stronger external source, so no fix needed. 'Decoupled-DMD' distillation also corroborated by third-party coverage.

black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev resolves: 32B rectified-flow transformer, unified generation+editing, multi-reference, FLUX Non-Commercial License (commercial_use:no CORRECT). The HF card did not surface the 'Qwen3 text embedder' / '4K' specifics on the front page, but FLUX.2's Qwen3-VL-based text encoder is well-documented elsewhere and not load-bearing. 18GB min on a 5090 implies 4-bit, which is the documented path — plausible. The 'successor to Pony-V6 anime workflow' framing is editorial but defensible.

github.com/HiDream-ai/HiDream-I1 resolves: 17B parameters, MIT License, Sparse Diffusion Transformer foundation model, with Full(50)/Dev(28)/Fast(16)-step tiers — all confirmed on the repo. MIT on a 17B model is genuinely notable and correctly highlighted. The 'MoE + dual-stream MMDiT + single-stream DiT' architecture detail is consistent with the published design. 16GB at full precision is tight for 17B but feasible on a 32GB card; plausible.

research.notes:
RE-DOWNLOAD GUIDE for a 32 GB RTX 5090, mid-2026. Training cutoff ~Jan 2026, so all claims below were re-verified via official HF/GitHub model cards + release notes in June 2026. TOP-LINE RECOMMENDATION (download both): (1) Microsoft TRELLIS.2-4B (Dec 2025, MIT, fully commercial-safe) as the new SOTA generalist, and (2) Tencent Hunyuan3D-2.1 (Jun 2025) as the production PBR-texture workhorse. They complement each other: TRELLIS.2 wins on arbitrary/complex topology and clean MIT licensing; Hunyuan3D-2.1 wins on photoreal PBR texture synthesis and has the deepest ComfyUI ecosystem. The 5090's 32 GB runs the full shape+texture pipeline of both comfortably (Hunyuan3D-2.1 full pipe peaks ~29 GB; TRELLIS.2 needs >=24 GB). LICENSING IS THE KEY DIVIDE for commercial game-asset work:
- MIT / Apache-2.0 (NO territory or user-count limits): TRELLIS.2, original TRELLIS, Direct3D-S2, PartCrafter (all MIT); Step1X-3D (Apache-2.0). These are the cleanest for selling game assets worldwide.
- Tencent Hunyuan community license (BOTH Hunyuan3D-2 and 2.1): commercial use IS allowed WITH attribution ("Created with Hunyuan3D"), BUT the license "Territory" explicitly EXCLUDES the European Union, the United Kingdom, and South Korea, and requires a separate Tencent license if your product exceeds 1,000,000 monthly active users. Source: https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hunyuan3D-2.1/blob/main/LICENSE. If the owner sells/operates in the EU/UK/South Korea, prefer the MIT/Apache models or email hunyuan3d@tencent.com for a regional license. The generated MESH itself is generally usable, but the model license terms are what bind distribution — read before shipping a commercial title in those regions. DEPENDENCY GOTCHA (both TRELLIS versions): the model code is MIT, but the OPTIONAL rendering/baking utilities pull in NVIDIA nvdiffrast/nvdiffrec, which carry a 1-way non-commercial NVIDIA source license. Mesh generation does not require commercial use of those libs, but if you bake textures with them in a commercial pipeline, swap in an MIT-licensed renderer. Source: https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2/issues/22 NOT AVAILABLE TO DOWNLOAD (do not waste time hunting weights): Hunyuan3D-2.5 (10B, 1024 geo res, 4K textures, ~Apr 2025) and Hunyuan3D-PolyGen (clean quad/tri retopo, Jul 2025) are API/cloud-only as of June 2026 — Tencent has NOT open-sourced their weights despite community requests (GitHub issue #111). They are the strongest Hunyuan tier and the only one that outputs game-ready quad topology, so they are worth knowing about for cloud bursts, but the open re-download stack tops out at Hunyuan3D-2.1. GAME-ASSET REALITY CHECK (applies to ALL of these): every current image/text-to-3D model outputs dense, organic, NON-quad triangle meshes (marching-cubes / sparse-voxel surfaces) with no clean edge loops and auto-unwrapped UVs. They are excellent for high-poly source, photogrammetry-style props, kit-bash blanks, and rapid concepting, but you MUST plan a retopo + UV pass (Blender QuadRemesher/Quad Remesh, InstaLOD, or ZBrush ZRemesher) before they are animation/engine-ready hero assets. PartCrafter is the exception in spirit — it splits output into separate semantic part meshes, which is the single biggest workflow win for kit-bashing and per-part materials. For truly engine-ready quads you currently need Hunyuan3D-PolyGen (cloud) or a manual/AI retopo step. COMFYUI STATUS: all open models below have working ComfyUI custom-node wrappers; Hunyuan3D-2/2.0-MV is the only one with native (built-in) ComfyUI support. TRELLIS.2 wrappers (visualbruno/ComfyUI-Trellis2 and PozzettiAndrea/ComfyUI-TRELLIS2) are Windows-11-tested with FP8 variants and tiled decoding for 32 GB cards, but require gated access to Meta's DINOv3 weights (request on HF) — flag this before download.

models.name: TRELLIS.2-4B
models.base_arch: Flow-matching DiT + Sparse 3D VAE ('O-Voxel' field-free sparse voxels)
models.summary: Microsoft's late-2025 successor to TRELLIS and the current open-weights SOTA for single-image-to-3D. A 4B flow-matching transformer over a 'field-free' sparse-voxel (O-Voxel) latent that handles arbitrary topology (open surfaces, thin walls, non-manifold geometry) and outputs textured GLB with full PBR (base color, metallic, roughness, opacity). MIT-licensed = clean for commercial game assets. Runs on the 5090: needs >=24 GB; FP8 ComfyUI variants + tiled decoder give headroom on 32 GB. ComfyUI via visualbruno/ComfyUI-Trellis2 and PozzettiAndrea/ComfyUI-TRELLIS2 (Windows-11 tested) but requires gated Meta DINOv3 access. Caveat: raw meshes are dense tris, not watertight (hole-filling scripts provided) and not aesthetically RLHF-tuned, so budget a retopo/UV pass for hero assets.
models.license: MIT (model + code). Note: optional nvdiffrast/nvdiffrec deps are non-commercial NVIDIA license.
models.commercial_notes: MIT on the model and inference code — commercial use, redistribution, and fine-tuning all permitted with no territory or MAU limit. Only watch-out: if you use the bundled nvdiffrast/nvdiffrec rendering utilities in a commercial pipeline, those carry NVIDIA's 1-way non-commercial source license; substitute an open renderer for baking.
models.speed_note: On H100: ~3s at 512^3, ~17s at 1024^3, ~60s at 1536^3. On a 5090 expect well under a minute for typical 1024^3 props; the fastest high-quality open option for batch/iterate.

best_for.purpose: Rapid concepting / batch iterating on props before committing to retopo
Game props with complex/hollow/thin-wall topology
Environment kit-bashing blanks (high-poly source)
Marketing hero renders from a single concept image

sources.claim: TRELLIS.2-4B is a 4B-param single-image-to-3D model under MIT license, requires a >=24 GB NVIDIA GPU, outputs GLB meshes with full PBR (base color, roughness, metallic, opacity), and runs ~3s/17s/60s at 512^3/1024^3/1536^3 on H100.

TRELLIS.2 uses a field-free O-Voxel sparse representation for arbitrary topology, released Dec 2025 (arXiv 2512.14692), outputs textured GLB with PBR, raw meshes may have small holes and are not watertight by default.

Geometry source to texture separately (Hunyuan/Step1X paint)
Sculpt/3D-print base meshes

models.name: PartCrafter
models.base_arch: Compositional latent Diffusion Transformer (jointly denoises multiple part latents)
models.summary: A genuinely different and very game-relevant tool: from ONE RGB image it generates multiple SEPARATE, semantically-distinct part meshes in a single shot (no manual segmentation) — e.g. a character split into body/armor/weapon, or a vehicle into chassis/wheels/turret. This is the biggest workflow unlock for kit-bashing and per-part materials/animation, since you get editable parts instead of one fused blob. Single-image-to-3D, GLB output (geometry-focused), scales to ~8-16 parts. Extremely light: runs from ~8 GB VRAM (reduce parts/tokens to save memory), trivial on a 32 GB 5090. MIT-licensed = commercial-clean. No official ComfyUI node yet (standalone Python). Situational but high-value alongside a texture model.
models.commercial_notes: MIT — commercial use permitted with no territory or user-count restriction (confirmed in the repo).
models.speed_note: Generates all parts in 'seconds' from one image; very light VRAM. Reduce part/token count to fit smaller GPUs (not needed on a 5090).

best_for.purpose: Part-segmented meshes for kit-bashing and per-part swaps
Characters/vehicles needing separable parts for animation/material assignment
Editable concept assets from a single image
Textured marketing renders (geometry-focused, weak alone)

sources.claim: PartCrafter (open-sourced 2025-07-13, NeurIPS 2025) is MIT-licensed, generates multiple separate part meshes (GLB) from a single RGB image, scales ~8-16 parts, and needs a CUDA GPU with >=8 GB VRAM.

verify.summary: Exceptionally strong submission. All 7 downloadable models plus the cloud-only warning item exist and resolve via retrieval, and nearly every field (license, params, architecture, VRAM, output formats) is backed by the repo/model card. The Tencent license claim that looked wrong on first search ("1M MAU cap") is actually CORRECT — verified against the raw LICENSE file (a competing search result conflated it with the 100M figure from a different Tencent license). VRAM figures are sane for a 32 GB card throughout and several match the source READMEs to the gigabyte (Hunyuan3D-2.1 29GB, Hunyuan3D-2 16GB, Step1X-3D 27GB, Direct3D-S2 24GB@1024). Only nits: one extra (PozzettiAndrea node) is cited via a grokipedia.com URL instead of its real GitHub repo, and the "native built-in ComfyUI" framing for Hunyuan3D-2 is defensible but the repo README itself only lists community wrappers. Currency is good — these are the 2025-2026 open SOTA. Missing tier: Hi3DGen (geometry leader), TripoSG/TripoSR (the VAE PartCrafter builds on + the speed tier), Stable Fast 3D.

verdicts.note: Verified at github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2 and HF microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B. MIT license, 4B params, O-Voxel field-free sparse-voxel + DiT/Sparse-3D-VAE, >=24GB VRAM, PBR outputs (base color/roughness/metallic/opacity), 512-1536 res — all stated on source. DINOv3 gating caveat is accurate but belongs to the ComfyUI route (visualbruno node README states 'You need access to facebook dinov3 models to use Trellis.2'); the base HF card does not mention DINOv3, and the claim correctly attributes the gating to the ComfyUI path, not the model itself.

Verified at github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1. Two-stage Shape-v2-1 (3.3B) + Paint-v2-1 (2B) PBR. VRAM matches exactly: shape 10GB, texture 21GB, shape+texture 29GB — fits 32GB. License is the Tencent Hunyuan Community License with EU/UK/South Korea exclusion AND a 1-million-MAU request threshold; I verified the '1M' figure against the actual LICENSE text ('greater than 1 million monthly active users... You must request a license'). A WebSearch summary claiming 100M was a conflation with a different Tencent license and is wrong — the researcher's 1M is correct. commercial_use 'conditional' is the right characterization.

verdicts.fixes: The 'ONE model with NATIVE (built-in) ComfyUI support' claim is only partly supported by the source. Native image-to-3D + multiview support landed in ComfyUI core (blog.comfy.org/p/hunyuan3d-20-and-muitiview-native), so the claim is defensible, but the Hunyuan3D-2 repo README itself attributes ComfyUI usage to COMMUNITY wrappers (ComfyUI-Hunyuan3DWrapper, ComfyUI-3D-Pack), not a first-party node. Soften 'native (built-in)' to 'supported in ComfyUI core'. Everything else verified: 2mv (1.1B) and 2mini (0.6B) variants exist; VRAM 6GB shape / 16GB shape+texture matches the README exactly; same Tencent license (EU/UK/KR exclusion, 1M MAU).

verdicts.note: Verified at github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS. MIT, image-large is 1.2B, SLAT (Structured Latents) rectified-flow transformer, >=16GB VRAM, decodes to 3D Gaussians + radiance fields + meshes with GLB/PLY export, CVPR'25 Spotlight — every claim matches the README. 'Superseded by TRELLIS.2 on fidelity/topology but uniquely versatile on output formats' is an accurate positioning.

Verified at github.com/stepfun-ai/Step1X-3D. Apache-2.0, hybrid VAE-DiT geometry 1.3B -> watertight TSDF + SD-XL-based texture 3.5B (6.1B total), 27GB VRAM for geometry+texture @50 steps (matches '~27 GB'), explicit LoRA fine-tuning section in training code, GLB/OBJ/PLY. ComfyUI is on the roadmap and NOT yet released — confirmed accurate as of the repo's latest news. Apache licensing covering EU/UK/Korea is the correct differentiator vs Tencent.

verdicts.fixes: Minor: the architecture is a sparse-VOLUME DiT operating on SDF (signed distance function) volumetric representation, not a generic mesh generator — the README frames it around SDF at up to 1024^3. The claim's 'high-fidelity meshes' is fine as user-facing output but the underlying repr is SDF; geometry-only (no PBR) is correct. All other fields verified: NeurIPS 2025, MIT, Spatial Sparse Attention, VRAM ~10GB@512 / ~24GB@1024 matches README, fits 32GB at full res.

verdicts.note: Verified at github.com/wgsxm/PartCrafter (2.4k stars). MIT, compositional latent DiT that finetunes the DiT while keeping TripoSG's VAE fixed, generates multiple semantically-distinct part meshes from one RGB image in a single shot, >=8GB VRAM, up to 16 parts, GLB output — all confirmed on the README. The kit-bashing / per-part-materials value framing is accurate and the model is genuinely differentiated.

Correctly flagged as a 'do not hunt for weights' warning. Verified via issue #111 (github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1/issues/111): user asks Tencent to open-source 2.5 + PolyGen weights/code; no official Tencent release, still cloud/API-only via 3d.hunyuan.tencent.com. 2.5 tech report (arXiv 2506.16504) June 2025, PolyGen July 2025 (auto-retopology, Tencent's ~70% time / ~35% topology claims). 10B/1024-geo/4K-PBR specs are as Tencent published. min_vram_gb=0 correctly signals 'not local'. Accurate framing.

extras.name: TTS Audio Suite (diodiogod/TTS-Audio-Suite)
extras.note: THE unified ComfyUI TTS hub to install first — one node set wraps ~13 engines (Chatterbox + Chatterbox Multilingual, F5-TTS, IndexTTS-2, Qwen3-TTS, CosyVoice3, Higgs Audio 2, VibeVoice, Step Audio EditX, Echo-TTS, MOSS-TTS, RVC voice conversion, plus Granite/Qwen3 ASR). Adds SRT/subtitle timing, multi-character switching via [CharacterName] tags, [language:character] switching, per-segment seed/temperature/CFG overrides, pause tags, and RVC training. Lets you A/B engines in one workflow instead of installing each separately. Best single starting point for the voice side of the rig.

extras.name: F5-TTS
extras.note: Very high-quality zero-shot voice cloning (flow-matching DiT, clones from 5-15s reference, RTF ~0.15, fits well under 24GB). BUT licensing blocks commercial use: code is MIT, pretrained WEIGHTS are CC-BY-NC due to the Emilia training dataset. Excellent for personal/research/prototyping VO; do NOT ship its output commercially. Strong ComfyUI support (niknah/ComfyUI-F5-TTS) and included in TTS-Audio-Suite. Recommend Chatterbox instead for any commercial game/marketing VO.

extras.name: IndexTTS-2
extras.note: Best-in-class EMOTION control (Sep 2025): disentangles timbre from emotion so you can mix one speaker's voice identity with another's emotional delivery, plus duration control ideal for video dubbing/lip-sync. License is restrictive (non-commercial without contacting the authors) with documented 'licensing pitfalls' — treat as non-commercial. Use for expressive prototyping; verify licensing before any commercial use. Available via TTS-Audio-Suite in ComfyUI.

extras.name: Qwen3-TTS
extras.note: Strong 2026 multilingual TTS with voice-design and emotion control (12Hz tokenizer + vocoder-free ConvNet decoder). Labeled Apache-2.0 BUT the license text adds a non-standard clause: 'This model must not be used to improve other AI models.' Still broadly commercial-friendly for VO output, just not a vanilla Apache-2.0. A good Chatterbox alternative for Asian-language (esp. Japanese-optimized) VO. In ComfyUI via TTS-Audio-Suite.

extras.name: VibeVoice (microsoft + community fork)
extras.note: Long-form multi-speaker TTS — up to ~90 minutes with up to 4 distinct speakers, MIT-licensed. Best open option for podcast/audiobook/long-cutscene dialogue. Microsoft briefly pulled the repo in early 2026 over cloning-misuse concerns, then re-enabled it with an audible AI disclaimer + watermark; a community fork (vibevoice-community/VibeVoice) exists. In ComfyUI via TTS-Audio-Suite. Note the embedded audible disclaimer may matter for polished commercial VO.

extras.name: MusicGen (Meta / AudioCraft)
extras.note: The 2023-era baseline (CC-BY-NC weights = non-commercial; code MIT). Largely superseded by ACE-Step 1.5 and Stable Audio 3.0 on quality, controllability, and licensing. Skip for this re-download unless you have a specific legacy workflow — it's neither the best quality nor commercial-safe. Listed only so it's explicitly deprioritized.

extras.name: kijai/ComfyUI-MMAudio
extras.note: The ComfyUI wrapper for MMAudio video-to-audio foley (weights hosted by Kijai on HF). Install if you want video-synced foley in-graph — but remember MMAudio weights are CC-BY-NC (non-commercial), so use for temp/prototype tracks, not shipped commercial audio.

research.notes:
RIG FIT: 32 GB VRAM is generously oversized for every model here — none are VRAM-constrained (the heaviest, HunyuanVideo-Foley XXL and YuE-7B, sit at ~16-20GB). So on this rig the differentiator is LICENSE + QUALITY, not whether it fits. Quantization is irrelevant for audio at this VRAM tier; run everything at full/bf16. RE-DOWNLOAD PRIORITY (commercial-safe core, install these first):
1. ACE-Step 1.5 (4B XL) — music/songs, MIT, LoRA-trainable house style. The flagship.
2. Chatterbox + Chatterbox Multilingual (+Turbo) — voice/VO, MIT, frontier quality.
3. Kokoro-82M — lightweight consent-free narration/UI voice, Apache-2.0.
4. Stable Audio 3.0 (Small+Medium) — game SFX/ambience, commercial under $1M revenue, licensed training data.
5. TTS Audio Suite (ComfyUI) — the unified node hub that wraps the voice engines. LICENSING IS THE STORY (call out clearly to the owner):
- COMMERCIAL-SAFE, clean: ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT), Chatterbox (MIT), Kokoro (Apache-2.0), YuE (Apache-2.0), VibeVoice (MIT, audible-disclaimer caveat).
- COMMERCIAL under a revenue threshold: Stable Audio 3.0 and Stable Audio Open 1.0 (free commercial under US $1M annual revenue via Stability Community License — fine for an indie; re-verify the LICENSE text).
- COMMERCIAL with regional/scale carve-outs: HunyuanVideo-Foley (Tencent Community License — excludes EU/UK/South Korea entities, 100M-MAU cap).
- NON-COMMERCIAL weights (prototype only, do NOT ship): MMAudio (CC-BY-NC), F5-TTS (CC-BY-NC, Emilia data), IndexTTS-2 (restrictive/contact-required), MusicGen (CC-BY-NC).
- LICENSE CAVEAT (commercial but non-standard clause): Qwen3-TTS ('must not be used to improve other AI models'). VOICE-CONSENT FLAG (legal, separate from software license): an MIT/Apache license on a cloning model does NOT grant rights to a person's VOICE. For commercial game/ad VO, only clone voices you own, have licensed, or that are synthetic. Chatterbox and VibeVoice embed watermarks (provenance, good). Kokoro avoids the issue entirely (fixed preset voices, no cloning) — the safest path when you don't need a specific voice. DATES/CONFIDENCE: Verified via official model cards/repos + Comfy blog + 2026 benchmark posts. ACE-Step 1.5 (Jan 2026 line, v0.1.8 May 2026), Stable Audio 3.0 (May 21 2026 day-0 ComfyUI), Chatterbox Turbo/Multilingual (2026) all post-date my training cutoff and were confirmed live via search. The Stability $1M revenue threshold and the Tencent EU/UK/SK + 100M-MAU carve-outs are standard terms for those license families but the exact current text should be re-read before shipping at scale. F5-TTS and MMAudio non-commercial status confirmed directly from their GitHub README license sections.

verify.summary: Retrieval-grounded fact-check of 9 audio-generation models + 7 extras. Overall the list is strong and accurate for a 32 GB RTX 5090: every model resolves to a real repo/page, all major architecture and VRAM claims check out, and the licensing characterizations are largely correct. 6 of 9 confirmed outright; 3 confirmed-with-fixes for currency/precision nits (Kokoro's #1 ranking is now superseded; HunyuanVideo-Foley's license-restriction text could not be confirmed verbatim from the repo page; ACE-Step's repo_url points to a real but slightly-off variant of the canonical repo name and the 'MIT weights' claim has minor conflicting secondary sourcing though the authoritative HF repo confirms MIT). Stable Audio 3.0 is genuinely real (released 2026-05-20). Notable domain omission: DiffRhythm/DiffRhythm 2 (Apache-2.0 full-song generator, a direct peer to ACE-Step/YuE).

verdicts.fixes: repo_url 'github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5' resolves and is the actively-maintained repo (self-described as 'the most powerful local music generation model'); the canonical weights repo is HF 'ACE-Step/Ace-Step1.5'. The 'MIT code AND weights' claim is BACKED by the HF model repo (license tag: mit) — but one secondary blog (efficienist) claimed the XL tier uses a 'StepFun proprietary license'; the authoritative HF page shows MIT for all variants, so treat the MIT-weights claim as confirmed but re-verify the XL LICENSE file text before scaling commercially. VRAM: claim 'min 6GB' + 'far under 32GB at 4B XL' is correct (repo: 2B turbo runs ≤6GB; 4B XL is ~9GB bf16, ~12GB with offload / ~20GB without). ComfyUI: native support confirmed but the announcement was 2026-03-20 (blog.comfy.org) — 'landed day-1' is loose marketing, not literal.
verdicts.note: DiT + AR LM front-end, text/lyrics-to-song, 10s–10min — all confirmed by repo. Strongest open local music model claim is well-supported.

verdicts.fixes: Real and recent — released 2026-05-20 (Stability news post + multiple outlets). repo_url 'stability.ai/stable-audio' resolves and correctly describes 3.0; note it is a marketing landing page, NOT a code repo (no public GitHub training repo) — the open weights live on HuggingFace (3.0 Small, Small SFX, Medium). Family is Small/Small SFX (459M), Medium (1.4B), Large (2.7B); Small + Medium are the open-weight tiers. License = Stability AI Community License with the $1M revenue threshold (confirmed verbatim). min_vram 4GB plausible (small models run on-device). commercial_use 'conditional' correct.
verdicts.note: DiT latent diffusion + T5 conditioning, music+SFX+ambience, up to ~6:20 — confirmed.

HF page confirms every claim: Stability AI Community License ($1M threshold), DiT latent diffusion + t5-base, up to 47s stereo @ 44.1kHz, 1B params. Model card explicitly states it is 'better at generating sound effects and field recordings than music' — the claim's characterization is accurate. License formal name is 'Stability AI Community License Agreement' (claim wrote 'Stable Audio Community License' — close enough, same agreement).

verdicts.fixes: Repo confirmed (6.3k stars), Apache 2.0 confirmed (explicitly permits commercial use of outputs), LLaMA-style AR backbone + audio tokens, lyrics2song with vocals+accompaniment. VRAM nuance: claim says 7B '~16GB at fp16, comfortable on 32GB' — defensible, but the repo's own guidance is more conservative ('24GB or less: run ≤2 sessions to avoid OOM'; 'full song generation: ≥80GB' for the unconstrained path). On 32GB it runs fine with sessioning/quantization; the YuEGP ~6GB fork is real. The 16GB figure is optimistic but not wrong for fp16 weights alone.
verdicts.note: Two-stage (s1-7B semantic + s2-1B acoustic). Apache option alongside MIT ACE-Step is a fair framing.

Repo confirmed (2.2k stars). Code MIT / weights CC-BY-NC 4.0 confirmed verbatim — commercial_use 'no' is correct. Multimodal flow-matching, video-to-audio AND text-to-audio, ~6GB in 16-bit. 'Prototyping/temp-track only' caveat is the right call given CC-BY-NC weights.

verdicts.fixes: Repo confirmed (1k stars), Tencent Hunyuan Community License present (LICENSE file exists). VRAM tiers confirmed EXACTLY: XXL 20GB (12GB with --enable_offload), XL 16GB (8GB offload) — matches claim. Multimodal diffusion w/ representation alignment, video(+text)-to-foley @ 48kHz confirmed. CAVEAT: the specific commercial restrictions cited (excludes EU/UK/South Korea entities, 100M MAU cap) are standard Tencent Hunyuan Community License terms and are PLAUSIBLE, but the repo page surfaced via fetch did not state them verbatim — the claim itself flags 'verify against your situation,' which is the correct posture. License_status set to unverified specifically on the geographic/MAU restriction text, not the license name.
verdicts.note: commercial_use 'conditional' is the right characterization for the Tencent community license.

Repo confirmed, MIT confirmed. Zero-shot cloning, exaggeration/emotion control, Perth neural watermark, 23-language Multilingual variant, Turbo variant — all confirmed. Blind-test stat is ACCURATE: published study shows Chatterbox-Turbo 65.3% vs ElevenLabs 24.5% (claim said ~65% vs ~25%); a separate base-model study shows 63.75%. ~5GB VRAM plausible (Turbo 350M, others 500M params). Consent caveat appropriately noted.

verdicts.fixes: All static facts confirmed by HF page: Apache 2.0, 82M params, StyleTTS2-derived (+ISTFTNet, non-autoregressive), fixed preset voices / NO cloning, 54 voices across 8 languages (claim said '54+ / 9 languages' — HF v1.0 states 8 languages; minor overcount). CURRENCY FIX: the 'hit #1 on TTS Arena in Jan 2026' claim is TRUE for that date, but it is no longer #1 — current TTS Arena/Artificial Analysis boards have it ~4th among open-weight models (Elo ~1062), well behind newer commercial models (Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, Sonic 3.5, etc.). The dated historical claim stands; present-tense 'the efficiency king' is still fair on params-per-quality, but it is no longer the outright leaderboard leader.
verdicts.note: Still an excellent CPU-capable lightweight workhorse; the value proposition (leaves the 5090 free) is intact. ~1GB at fp16 confirmed plausible.

missing.name: DiffRhythm / DiffRhythm 2 (ASLP-lab)
missing.why: The most significant omission. Apache-2.0 (fully permissive, like YuE) end-to-end full-length song generation with synchronized vocals+accompaniment via VAE+DiT latent diffusion — generates ~4:45 songs in ~10s, and DiffRhythm 2 (block flow matching) improves fidelity. It is a direct peer to ACE-Step 1.5 and YuE in exactly the 'open local full-song' niche this list centers on, and arguably the fastest of the three. Belongs as a third song engine alongside ACE-Step (MIT) and YuE (Apache).

missing.name: VibeVoice (Microsoft)
missing.why: Listed only as an extra, but warrants promotion to a primary TTS entry: MIT-licensed, 47.6k stars, and uniquely strong at LONG multi-speaker conversational synthesis (TTS-1.5B does up to ~90 min, up to 4 speakers) plus a 0.5B ~300ms realtime streaming model and a 7B ASR. For dialogue-heavy game VO / podcast-style narration this fills a gap Chatterbox and Kokoro don't (long multi-speaker conversation). Note the deepfake-misuse warning.

missing.name: AudioGen / Stable Audio's SFX peers — covered; main gap is a dedicated TTS like F5-TTS already noted
missing.why: Minor — F5-TTS is already in extras (correctly flagged non-commercial: MIT code but CC-BY-NC pretrained weights due to the Emilia dataset). Flagging it here only to confirm the extras classification is correct; not a true omission. The genuine must-add remains DiffRhythm.

research.domain: Local LLMs (Ollama) + vision/captioning + prompt-enhancement for a ComfyUI game-asset and marketing pipeline on RTX 5090 (32 GB VRAM), as of 2026-06-02

models.name: Qwen3.6-27B
models.base_arch: Qwen3.6 dense transformer
models.commercial_notes: Apache 2.0 - unrestricted commercial use, fine-tuning, and redistribution. No MAU cap, no attribution requirement. Safest possible license for game-asset commercial work.
models.speed_note: On 32 GB you can run Q8 (~28-30 GB) for near-lossless quality, or Q6_K (~22 GB) with comfortable KV-cache headroom for the 256K context. Q4_K_M is ~17 GB and very fast. This is the single best general pick for a 32 GB card in mid-2026.
models.summary: The flagship general-purpose pick. A 27B dense model that posts SWE-bench Verified 77.2% (within ~3.7 pts of Claude Opus 4.6) and matches Claude 4.5 Opus on Terminal-Bench 2.0, beating the previous 397B Qwen3.5 MoE on coding. Unified thinking/non-thinking checkpoint (`think:false` for low-latency calls), 256K context, 201 languages. Excellent at coding, reasoning, chat, AND prompt-rewriting in one model. Note: the base weights are multimodal-capable via a separate mmproj, but the Ollama build ships text-only.

best_for.purpose: General reasoning, chat, and agentic workflows
Local coding agent / repo-level work (ComfyUI custom nodes, pipeline scripts)
Prompt enhancement / rewriting for image gen (strong instruction following + creative writing)
Marketing copy, product descriptions, multilingual content

One-command Ollama install (`ollama run gemma4`).

It exists specifically to caption images for training/fine-tuning diffusion models, with mature ComfyUI integration. Choose it over CapRL/Qwen3-VL when you need full content coverage or tag-style output; choose CapRL when you want the absolute best dense natural-language captions under a clean Apache license.
